meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about the zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it? And what do you actually have?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

Turn the screen; I read documents myself. I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Owen wrote that essay over the weekend, and pasting finished work into a new file at night proves nothing about where it was written.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

Give me the text, Hale; I'm searching it myself. A misquoted line is a mistake a tired seventeen-year-old makes, nothing more. Whatever happens from here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Procedure 4.4, I have it in front of me. Thursday at 8:15, in your room, no other students, and I want in writing tonight that nothing is on his file now and nothing goes on it after. If that email arrives, he'll do it, to put this behind him.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, and that if it holds up the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I still require written confirmation that nothing is on his file now, that nothing goes on it afterward, and that no other students will be present. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to the supervised rewrite on Thursday morning in your room, and she still wants written confirmation that nothing is on his file and nothing will be added.
What moved her: "That line is not in Hamlet." It was specific, tied to the essay itself, and something she could check on her own.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, answer that directly before you show the version history, so her procedural question doesn't stay open.
